title: Balance Point? Centre of Gravity Explained Simply | Class 11 Physics
description:
A tightrope walker carries a long pole. A truck piled high with hay tips over on a turn. A toy bird balances on its beak. And Aarav cannot find where his cardboard cut-out balances on a pencil tip. All of these hide one special point: the centre of gravity. In this animated lesson for Class 11 Physics (Chapter 6, System of Particles and Rotational Motion) we find it with a plumb line, in two tries.

On a live motion notebook the cut-out hangs on a pin and swings to rest, while the readout tracks the angle, the lever arm and the turning effect of the weight, and a graph shows that turning effect dying away to zero. A slow-mo replay freezes the swing to show weight times lever arm. Two plumb lines cross at G. We prove step by step why the centre of gravity matches the centre of mass when g is the same everywhere, see link by link why the plumb line works, compare a cardboard cut-out with a very tall tower, and see when a box or a bus tips over. Then a worked tipping-angle example, the exam trap (G can lie outside the body), an original JEE Main pattern question, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for NCERT, CBSE, ISC (CISCE) and PUC (Karnataka) Class 11 students, and for JEE Main and NEET preparation.
